reasoning: The plan is the issue's scope with no new script, every platform behaviour it rests on is observed, the dropped row has a traceable catcher in every clone, and after the rework every clause of the spec deltas — including the exit-1 guard and the `.git/hooks` footprint — is asserted by a named test in the map.

simpler.evidence: Each decision carries its rejected alternative: D1 (keep the row for every clone) rejected because it duplicates the planned line in a dry-run and is false after a confirmed one; D3 (treat a foreign hook as blocked) rejected against pre-commit's own migration mode; D4 (a new standalone hook script) rejected as a second managed file and settings entry for the same session-start moment. The whole-change alternative 'marker only, no installer step' is not weighed in design.md, but #270's Brief asks for both paths explicitly (installer step, blocked row, other-clone marker, tests for both), so the plan is the issue's scope and not more: no new file, no new script, no new dependency, one reader shared by the step and the row, and the step reuses the existing `Step`/`apply` shape of init.py.

map.evidence: All eleven delta scenarios have a map entry (tasks.md §Scenario → test map). Fresh repository → test_installed_footprint_is_closed for the working tree plus test_pre_push_hook_is_installed and test_foreign_pre_push_is_migrated for the `.git/hooks` half the requirement now admits; Installation of another release / Consumer render / Consumer file without the block → existing tests, marked unchanged; Hook installed in this clone → test_pre_push_hook_is_installed + test_foreign_pre_push_is_migrated; Install leaves no hook → test_pre_push_install_leaves_no_hook; Hook missing where nothing else is planned → test_nothing_to_install (extended in 1.2); Per-clone row → test_pre_push_blocked_is_manual (4 params); Hook missing → test_pre_push_missing_is_marked + test_pre_push_and_skill_markers_share_output + test_pre_push_id_matches_installer; Hook installed or not rendered → test_pre_push_silent; Hook state unreadable → test_pre_push_undecidable. No scenario is left without a test and no entry is `n/a`.

red.evidence: Group 1 holds four tasks: 1.1 harness (`LABELS` + injectable `which`), 1.2 installer tests, 1.3 check tests, 1.4 the constants-only stub in skill_check.py plus `check_red` over 14 node ids — now including test_pre_push_install_leaves_no_hook — with 'verify each fails in its body'. The stub makes the new-symbol tests fail in the body rather than at import, and test_pre_push_install_leaves_no_hook fails on its `exit 1` assertion before `_pre_push_step` exists. Task 1.1's `LABELS` edit also turns test_init.py::test_lifecycle and the resume test RED, which is consistent. `test_pre_push_id_matches_installer` is the only map test outside the check_red ids: task 1.4's stub gives skill_check the same ID constant, so it is green by construction — a pin of an existing constant (Risks: a pre-commit release changing the `# ID:` line), not a behavioural assertion. RED is committed before implementation in 1.4.

platform.evidence: Every platform behaviour the design rests on is observed, not asserted: `pre-commit install --hook-type pre-push` output, exit 0, the `# ID: 138fd403…` line and a second idempotent run; migration mode writing `.git/hooks/pre-push.legacy`; `[ERROR] Cowardly refusing to install hooks with core.hooksPath set.` with exit 1 — all three in proposal.md — Why, pre-commit 4.6.0, scratch repositories, 2026-09-30. D4 records the `pre-commit --help` listing of 4.6.0 (install, uninstall, init-templatedir, no status) as the standard-does-not-fit evidence, and what `init-templatedir` with `git config init.templateDir` does instead. The git reads (`git config --get core.hooksPath` exit 1 when unset, `git rev-parse --git-path hooks/pre-push`) are prior art shipped in manual.py `_pre_push`, and test_pre_push_blocked_is_manual[hooks-path] sets `core.hooksPath` in a real sandbox clone, so the exit-0 branch is exercised against real git. The SessionStart JSON shape (`systemMessage` + `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext`) is the shipped templates/skill_check.py of #187.

replaced.evidence: One guard is narrowed: the unconditional `manual pre-push` row disappears for a clone the run installs (or would install). D1 names why keeping it is wrong (duplicate line in a dry-run, false after a confirmed run) and D4 names what stops proving — the row was the only text telling the person that other clones need the step. Both losses are re-carried: the session-start marker in every clone (D4) and SKILL.md Install step 4 (task 3.2). No project-declared input is replaced by a caller-supplied one; `Target.pre_commit` and the harness `which` are injection of an already-used lookup, not a new input.

catcher.evidence: The catchers are traceable to concrete steps. (1) Missing hook in any other clone → `.claude/agent-process-check.py`, whose file and whose `hooks.SessionStart` entry in `.claude/settings.json` are consumer files the installation PR commits (init.py CHECK/SETTINGS steps), so every clone of the consumer runs it at each Claude session start and prints the marker with both commands — tests 1.3. (2) Missing hook in the clone init runs in, when blocked → the `manual pre-push` row of that run's own output (test_pre_push_blocked_is_manual) and the same session-start marker. (3) `pre-commit install` exiting non-zero → `ctx.call(check=True)` raises InstallError, `install()` prints `error: …` and returns 1. (4) The command exiting 0 without a hook → the re-read InstallError of D2, reached in `_perform` and now proven by test_pre_push_install_leaves_no_hook (exit 1, no `written pre-push`, the hook path named). (5) A drifting pre-commit `# ID:` line → both readers report the hook missing, visible, plus test_pre_push_id_matches_installer.

length.evidence: Spec words added: 'The installed footprint is closed' +21, 'Init renders the pre-push hook' +128 plus the +28 of the new scenario 'Install leaves no hook', 'A Claude session start reports a missing pre-push hook' +101 — about 278 words, and the tests of the map now assert all of them: the classification and the print order after onboarding-pr; the `pre-commit install --hook-type pre-push` call after the push and the installed ID line; the exit-1 guard with the hook path (test_pre_push_install_leaves_no_hook); the no-branch/commit/issue/push/PR clause (test_nothing_to_install); the blocked reason with both commands (4 params); the `.git/hooks` closure `{pre-push}` and `{pre-push, pre-push.legacy}`; and every word of the ADDED requirement — marker, reason, both commands, the two silent cases, the unreadable case and the shared output. Task 3.2's SKILL.md Install step 4 sentence is the docs half, verified by test_planning_workflow.py.

bespoke.evidence: The plan adds no script and no check of its own: it extends the existing installer step list and the existing installed SessionStart check. D4 records the decision for the second verdict — problem closed: #270, the silent gap the archived consumer-pre-push-hook design accepted; standard for the job: pre-commit 4.6.0 has no status command, and its `init-templatedir` route works only for future clones and through machine-wide git config, which is the shared-state change the change keeps out of scope; alternative (a standalone hook script) rejected. The one duplicated constant the self-contained template forces is pinned by test_pre_push_id_matches_installer.
